title: OCM Module Definition v1.1
description: Declarative self-description of an assembly-cell module. Consumed by motion planners, PLC code generators, and AI agents.

ocm_version.description: Spec version this manifest is written against. 1.1 adds: x-<name> custom protocols, pose6d/vec3/struct composite types.

revision.description: SemVer. MAJOR bump = breaking change to frames, capabilities, or signals.

license.description: SPDX identifier. Hardware modules should use CERN-OHL-S-2.0.

kind.description: Determines which sections are required. See allOf conditionals.

mount.description: How this module attaches to the cell base or to a robot flange.

interface.description: ocm-base-grid-50 = the cell base T-slot/bolt grid. iso-9409-1-* = robot tool flange.

footprint_mm.description: [x, y] envelope on the mounting plane.

keepout_mm.description: Service clearance required around the footprint. Cell layout validator enforces this.

frames.description: Named coordinate frames. 'origin' is REQUIRED and is the mounting datum; all other frames are relative to it.

tcp.description: Tool center point. REQUIRED for kind=end_effector.

visual.description: Path to display mesh (GLB preferred — renders directly in a three.js/R3F viewer).

collision.description: Path to collision mesh. Convex hull or convex decomposition STRONGLY preferred -- Tesseract's Bullet backend is far faster on convex geometry. ADR-0027: required when collision_source is 'authored' (and checked for envelope containment); ABSENT when 'derived' (the proxy is built from posed envelopes + structure primitives -- a mesh here would be the second artifact D1 exists to remove). ADR-0016: a DRAFT (revision 0.x) may omit this artifact claim.

urdf_fragment.description: Path to a URDF snippet declaring this module's links and joints. THIS IS THE KEY FIELD: it is what allows cell.yaml to compile straight into a Tesseract scene graph with zero manual CAD work.

collision_source.description: ADR-0027 D1: how this module's collision geometry is produced. `derived` -- the resolver builds the collision proxy from posed component envelopes plus mechanical.structure primitives; NO collision mesh artifact is declared. `authored` -- `collision` names a hand-produced mesh, authoritative, and checked for containment of every posed component envelope (D2). Required at publish (publish_module refuses without it -- the claim is producibility, ADR-0027 D6 amending ADR-0016 D3); a draft omits it until the choice is made (design, not a default). One mode per module.

located.description: ADR-0031 D3: this module locates a carrier against machined datum features. Lives on the LOCATING module (the conveyor), never on the carrier -- the datum features are machined into this module's structure and do not travel. Each constraint names a physical feature, the degrees of freedom it governs, and a per-feature tolerance; every one of the six DOF must be governed exactly once (OCM_LOCATED_DOF_UNGOVERNED / OCM_LOCATED_DOF_OVERCONSTRAINED), each governed DOF carries a tolerance (OCM_LOCATED_TOLERANCE_MISSING), and units are type-checked against the DOF (OCM_LOCATED_UNIT_MISMATCH). Tolerances are declared, not yet consumed -- a located pose without them is a claim of infinite precision.

frame.description: A frame in this module's own mechanical.frames: the pose a correctly seated carrier lands at (ADR-0031 D2 -- the ROOT of the carrier's chain, with transit a negative offset from it). Unknown refuses (OCM_LOCATED_FRAME_UNKNOWN).

feature.description: The physical feature doing the constraining, as the drawing names it (e.g. 'lift_stop_surface', 'locating_pins').

governs.description: Which degrees of freedom this feature constrains. Across all constraints, each of the six is governed exactly once -- ungoverned and doubly-governed are the same failure: a constraint scheme that does not close.

tolerance.description: Per governed DOF: how well this feature constrains it. Per feature, not per datum -- the plane and the pins are different features with genuinely different numbers, and averaging them would be an invented value.

source.description: Where these numbers came from -- ADR-0029's convention on durations, applied here. Required; never defaulted. Anything quoting a positional accuracy derived from this tolerance inherits the label.

com_mm.description: Center of mass in the origin frame. Needed for robot payload calc when kind=end_effector.

inertia_kgm2.description: [Ixx, Iyy, Izz, Ixy, Ixz, Iyz]. Optional; required for high-dynamic payloads.

structure.description: ADR-0027 D3: module-owned structure -- brackets, plates, standoffs -- declared as posed primitives. Fabricated parts have no datasheet and nothing to transcribe (ADR-0014); this is module-layer DESIGN, authored. It is what makes `derived` collision mode viable for a real assembly rather than only a rack of purchased devices.

path.description: mesh only: path to the fabricated part's own mesh -- we produce it, so we own the CAD (ADR-0027 D3).

units.description: Length unit for size/radius/length, resolved by ocm_core.units' explicit table (unrecognised -> OCM_UNIT_UNRECOGNISED). Required for box/cylinder.

pose.description: Pose in the owning link's frame; xyz in `units`, rpy in degrees.

link.description: ADR-0027 D4: the urdf_fragment link this primitive rides; defaults to the fragment root. A link absent from the fragment refuses (OCM_LINK_UNKNOWN).

pins.description: This connector's own pinout, as the source states it.

pin.description: Pin identifier as the datasheet labels it (e.g. '1', 'A', 'GND').

function.description: What this pin is for, as the source states it (e.g. '24VDC supply', 'output_1 signal').

protocol.description: Transport. Enumerated values have (or will have) toolchain drivers. x-<name> declares a custom/proprietary protocol: valid for authoring, resolving, scene and plan (which never touch transports); the runtime coordinator refuses to go live unless a driver is registered for it, naming the protocol. Escape hatch per ADR-0012.

esi.description: Path to EtherCAT ESI file / EDS / GSDML as applicable.

signals.description: The semantic I/O map. Names here become PLC tag names in generated code — so they must be meaningful, not IN_00/OUT_03.

name.description: snake_case. Becomes the generated PLC tag.

direction.description: Direction FROM THE PLC's point of view.

offset.description: Byte offset in the process image.

role.description: Binds a signal to its PackML meaning so the cell coordinator can be generated. Signals without a role are process data. handshake_* roles bind the spec/08 robot handshake contract to this module's transport.

frame.description: For type=pose6d: the frame this pose is expressed in, as '<instance-relative frame name>' resolved against this module's declared frames (or, in capability results, a frame of a plan-referenced instance, e.g. 'nest1.part_datum'). REQUIRED for pose6d — a pose without a frame is a bug waiting to happen.

fields.description: For type=struct: ordered field name -> scalar type. Wire layout is fields in declaration order.

source.description: ADR-0014: provenance into a components/ entry's own signal list, as 'REFDES.signal_name' (the refdes must appear in this module's own components: list). Optional -- a signal with no components: list, or one that isn't backed by a purchased part, has none.

capabilities.description: The verbs this module offers. This is the agent-facing surface — it is deliberately shaped like a tool schema.

summary.description: One line, plain English. The agent reads this.

parameters.description: Typed inputs. Ranges are HARD LIMITS — the generator must reject a plan that exceeds them, and the agent must never propose one.

motion.description: How the robot (or this module's own axes) must move to execute the op. Consumed directly by the planner.

frame.description: Which named frame does the work.

approach_vec.description: Unit vector in the working frame. e.g. [0,0,-1] = drive down along tool Z.

approach_mm.description: Standoff distance where the approach move begins.

clearance_mm.description: Collision-check inflation during the op. The planner adds this to the module's collision geometry.

hold_still.description: If true, the robot must be stationary during execution (screwdriving, press). If false, the op is executed ALONG a path (dispense, weld) and 'path' below applies.

path.description: For hold_still=false ops. Declares what the process needs of the path.

corner_radius_mm.description: Minimum blend radius the process tolerates. A dispense bead cannot survive a sharp corner at speed.

preconditions.description: Boolean expressions over this module's signals and cell state. The generator emits interlock logic from these — they are not documentation.

postconditions.description: What is true after a SUCCESSFUL execution. The agent uses these to chain operations.

results.description: Data the module returns. Becomes traceability records.

nominal_duration_s.description: For cycle-time estimation and takt balancing.

consumes.description: Consumable ids drawn down per execution (screws, adhesive volume). Feeds replenishment planning.

requires.description: ADR-0023: abstract boolean facts this capability needs, named without saying who provides them. The cell binds each key to a concrete `instance.signal`; a precondition may reference a key by name. Unbound at cell resolve -> OCM_REQUIREMENT_UNBOUND.

timeout_s.description: ADR-0023: how long before this op is wrong -- distinct from nominal_duration_s, and NOT overridable by a plan. On expiry the module is disposed per on_timeout.

on_timeout.description: ADR-0023: disposition when timeout_s expires. hold -> PackML Held (nothing damaged; operator clears and resumes). abort -> Abort (part compromised, routes to reject). hold on a capability whose state_machine.abort_safe is false refuses (OCM_TIMEOUT_DISPOSITION_CONFLICT).

actuates.description: ADR-0028 D1: the joints this verb drives and the value each holds when the postcondition is true -- the geometric half of the verb. Joint names are this module's own urdf_fragment's, unnamespaced. `to` is the endpoint only (no `from`: the precondition asserts where the machine was); `units` is REQUIRED and resolved through ocm_core.units, type-checked against the joint (D2 -- a bare number meaning metres-or-radians by context is the silent-plausible-value failure the refusal engine exists to exclude). Optional: a capability with no `actuates` moves nothing (D4), which is a legitimate description, not a gap.

joint.description: A joint name in this module's own urdf_fragment (unnamespaced). Unknown, fixed, or limit-violating targets refuse at resolve (OCM_ACTUATION_*).

to.description: The value the joint holds when the postcondition is true, in `units`.

units.description: Verbatim unit, resolved by ocm_core.units' explicit tables -- length for prismatic, angle for revolute/continuous; a mismatch refuses (OCM_ACTUATION_UNIT_MISMATCH).

process.description: Recipe-level parameters for kind=process modules. Distinct from capability parameters: these are set once per PART, not per operation.

warmup_s.description: Time from enable to process-ready. The cell coordinator must sequence this.

idle_timeout_s.description: Beyond this idle time, a purge is required before the next op. Adhesive skins over.

state_machine.description: MANDATORY. Every OCM module speaks PackML. This is what makes the cell coordinator generatable once instead of per-module.

implements.description: Which PackML states this module actually implements. Modules may omit Held/Suspended if they cannot be interrupted mid-op.

abort_safe.description: TRUE if the module can be aborted mid-execution without damaging the part or itself. A screwdriver mid-drive is NOT abort-safe; a gripper holding a part is not either. The cell coordinator must know this to sequence e-stop recovery.

safety.description: Declares hazards. Does NOT constitute a risk assessment and must never be treated as one.

required_performance_level.description: ISO 13849 PL required of the SAFETY circuit that guards this module.

sto_required.description: Module has an STO input that must be wired to the cell safety circuit.

safe_state.description: What the module does on loss of safety power. Must be described plainly.

components.description: ADR-0014: this module as an ASSEMBLY of purchasable components (spec/10). Optional -- a module with no components list stays valid (some purchased devices genuinely are whole modules). Derivable from this list: the purchasable BOM, power budget, air consumption.

refdes.description: Reference designator, e.g. 'VG1', 'IO1' -- this module's own name for this component instance.

ref.description: id@revision of a components/ entry. The referenced component must be published (revision >= 1.0.0), same as a module ref.

pose.description: Where this component instance sits in the module's own local scene (Modules-page authoring UI). Optional -- a components: entry with no pose is still valid.

link.description: ADR-0027 D4: the urdf_fragment link this component instance attaches to (a component riding a moving axis travels with it); defaults to the fragment root. NOT ADR-0015 D1's rejected STEP node-path binding -- link names are authored by us in our own fragment; one that does not exist refuses (OCM_LINK_UNKNOWN).

ports.description: ADR-0015: this module's own external interface, one entry per connection it exposes. A module declaring none stays valid. Choosing to present one 24V feed rather than three, or one air inlet rather than a manifold, is module-layer DESIGN (ADR-0014) -- a port is authored, never derived from a component.

id.description: This port's own name -- what a net/link endpoint's `port` field references.

role.description: Communication role, as the datasheet/design labels it -- 'IN'/'OUT' on an EtherCAT slave map to slave_in/slave_out.

nets.description: ADR-0015: electrical and pneumatic connectivity as NETS -- N unordered endpoints sharing one common node (a rail, a shared supply line). Optional; a module declaring neither key stays valid. Topology for communication is a LINK instead (below), not a net -- an EtherCAT chain's order can't be expressed by an unordered set.

links.description: ADR-0015: communication connectivity as LINKS -- exactly two endpoints (a cable between two ports), never an unordered net (order is what lets an EtherCAT chain's master/slave sequence be derived by walking a/b, later, at resolve time -- never stored here). Optional; a module declaring none stays valid.

then.description: A feeder MUST declare a 'pick' frame — where the part presents — and a capability that guarantees part presence.

dof_tolerance.description: ADR-0031 D3: one DOF's tolerance -- an explicit value and a verbatim unit, resolved through ocm_core.units' tables and type-checked against the DOF (length for x/y/z, angle for rx/ry/rz).

unit.description: Verbatim, e.g. 'mm' or 'deg' -- never convert; a unit in neither table refuses (OCM_UNIT_UNRECOGNISED), a unit in the wrong table for the DOF refuses (OCM_LOCATED_UNIT_MISMATCH).

rpy_deg.description: Fixed-axis roll-pitch-yaw, degrees. Matches URDF convention (which uses radians — the loader converts).

endpoint.description: ADR-0015: one end of a net or link. References EXISTING field names only, no renaming or alias layer -- `port` is a ports[].id, `refdes` is a components[].refdes, `ref`/`pin` are exactly what the referenced component's own connector/pin calls itself (ComponentConnector.ref, ComponentPin.pin -- see ocm-component-1.0.schema.json). Whether a given combination is actually valid for its domain (e.g. an unknown refdes, or a pin that connector doesn't have) is a resolve-time concern, not schema-enforced here.

ref.description: The referenced component's own connector name, exactly as its electrical.connectors[].ref or comms.connectors[].ref names it.

pin.description: Exactly as the connector's own pins[].pin names it.

net.description: ADR-0015: N unordered endpoints on a common node. `pressure`/`pressure_units` apply to a pneumatic net's own single operating point -- a module-layer DESIGN choice (ADR-0014); a component's own pneumatic range stays a range.

instance_pose.description: A component instance's own local pose within a module's assembly scene -- always relative to the module's own origin, never to a named frame (unlike $defs/frame, deliberately no parent/note here).

parameter.description: A typed, bounded, unit-carrying value. Bounds are enforced by the generator and respected by the agent.

summary.description: Plain English. The agent reads this to decide what to pass.

frame.description: For type=pose6d results/params: the reference frame. REQUIRED for pose6d.
